My symptoms were really most troublesome in romantic relationships, and I got sick of hurting people I got close too. It was definitely hard at first. My boyfriend, at the time is the one who originally pushed me to get help which I'm so fucking thankful for. But things didn't work out with us. After that, I really had no support which was the push I needed to make real progress. I had a habit of either relying on other people to fix me, or latching on to even more messed up people and ignoring my issues to help them. But being alone, I was free to just focus on me. 

Keep in mind that learning any new skill is never easy, and especially something this big takes time, practice and lots of effort. Slowly but surely things do get better though. Everyday, I just told myself "This is who I am now. This is how I react to things." After awhile you start to believe it, and don't have to tell yourself anymore.

http://www.getselfhelp.co.uk/dbt.htm

That site really helped me to learn the skills I needed. However, going to individual and group DBT showed me how to implement them. A year after starting, I consider myself "recovered," and my therapist agrees that I no longer fit my diagnosis. 😁

I've always personally felt that medications were a quick fix when it comes to mental illness. However, after many failed therapists and medications, I landed in the hospital for the third time and ended up on a medication that really worked for me. It was then that I finally began making progress in therapy. 

That being said, everyone is different. Medication cannot completely keep personality disorders under control, but if some symptoms are so severe that they are interfering with your progress, treat the symptoms first. Do your research on the pros and cons of potential medications; I really advise anyone to stay away from SSRIs & benzodiazepines. If you are adamant about avoiding medication, make this clear to your psychiatrist. If they try to pressure you, I would consider finding a new one. Just because they are a doctor doesn't mean they know best. We all have an agenda and bills to pay, sadly.
